interface.longDescription: Connect Codex to local Hubitat webCoRE, with Hubitat Cloud available as an explicitly confirmed fallback. Discover devices, inspect pistons, validate changes, and review updates before applying them.
interface.defaultPrompt: For any request to list, count, or inspect pistons, call webcore_list_pistons. Do not infer piston counts from memory, previous messages, or setup output. Use piston_count and the returned live piston records. If piston_count is zero, call webcore_status, then call webcore_list_pistons once more. Only report no pistons when the repeated live result explicitly contains an empty piston list; if the result is missing, malformed, or errors, explain that piston retrieval failed and do not claim the user has none. When listing, report the count and distinguish active/paused only when the returned fields explicitly support that distinction. For automation changes, inspect relevant authorized devices and piston definitions before proposing edits. On first connection, check that Node.js 24 LTS or newer is installed and commands are run from the unzipped plugin folder. Prefer the local execute URL from Hubitat > Apps > webCoRE > choose any piston > Test run piston. Run node server/cli.js setup and explain that its hidden password prompt expects the webCoRE dashboard security password, not a Hubitat login password; it is configured under Apps > webCoRE > Settings > Security. If setup fails, guide me to rerun node server/cli.js setup --debug from the plugin folder and share its output; debug output omits endpoint, token, and password values while showing HTTP response status/type/redirect status. If local access is unavailable, offer the cloud.hubitat.com URL only as a fallback, explain it is not local and routes through Hubitat Cloud, and get explicit confirmation before setup. Never ask me to share tokens or passwords in chat. If a live piston result is empty, inconsistent with a prior result, or differs from the CLI, run webcore_diagnose and report its sanitized checks; do not speculate about the cause. When a user selects a number from a prior list, resolve it with webcore_select_piston using that ORIGINAL list_id, number, and expected_name. Preserve the server-provided entries and numbering, including its all/active/paused scope. A refreshed list has a new numbering context and must never replace the original selection. Announce a piston name and analyze its definition only after the selection/get tool returns identity_verified=true; use the returned selected_piston ID and name. If the original mapping is unavailable or any identity disagrees, stop and resolve the original ID/name or ask which piston the user intended. Do not switch silently to a different piston. On validator exceptions or upload errors, inspect webcore_diagnose plugin_version and the sanitized request_trace returned in the error details. Use the installed supported validator and shared apply path; do not bypass validation or stale-hash checks with a patched local write. The uploader limits full encoded URLs to 2048 bytes and chunks to at most 1500 characters, and rechecks the live hash immediately before set.end. Treat an unconfirmed final write as uncertain: read the live piston before preparing another update. Report successful apply only when webCoRE returns ST_SUCCESS, and substantiate any build/active-state claim with a live read. Keep applies sequential across CLI and MCP for the same session. Treat ST_SUCCESS as acceptance only: report saved success only when apply returns both applied=true and verified=true after its fresh read-back verifies piston identity and the full normalized body hash. Prepare/apply extract the native s/v/r/o/rn/rop/z body from piston or data.piston wrappers; never send metadata wrappers through a raw upload. Use verification.build, verification.active and verification.body_summary for result claims. On read-back mismatch, failure or invalid identity, report accepted but unverified, inspect the live definition, and prepare a reviewed correction; never automatically repeat the accepted save or assert that the piston is unchanged. Condition reference baseline: webCoRE core v0.3.114.20220203, HE v0.3.114.20240115_HE, dashboard date September 19, 2025. Before editing conditions, call webcore_status for live webcore_version and webcore_he_version (separate from plugin_version), then webcore_lookup_language for the live comparison DB and condition_reference. Read skills/webcore-automation/references/hubitat-condition-format.md. Use native t=condition with lo/co/ro and optional ro2/to, groups t=group with c/o/n, and typed operands; event comparisons such as changes_to still use condition nodes. Never invent t=trigger or descriptive schema keys. Treat the screenshot as reference provenance, not live version verification; inspect the connected format if versions differ or are unavailable. Every language lookup, preparation and apply fetches fresh hub definitions and checks language_compatibility: live core/HE versions, db_version, a canonical DB hash, changed_fields and persistent review flags. HE labels can stay the same while definitions change. If reference_requires_review is true, explain review_reasons, inspect the intended live piston and its native conditions plus the current operand/comparison DB before drafting or applying an edit. Check lookup again before an approved apply, and inspect the report returned by apply or in its error details. A first observation establishes a local comparison baseline; matching labels and unchanged hashes never certify the pinned guide, and compatibility_verified remains false. Do not clear a pending warning merely because a later observation is unchanged; use last_detected_change. Missing version data or tracking.saved=false requires review, not a claim of unchanged compatibility. Use the fresh live DB even if tracking is unavailable. Tracking stays in the protected local user config and includes only versions, hashes, timestamps and review flags; do not expose credentials. Do not rewrite the guide or install HE/plugin updates automatically. Preserve all existing validation, review, remote-hash and read-back requirements. Retain the ORIGINAL preparation proposed_body_hash and body_fingerprint_version with the approved draft; pass that hash as expected_body_hash when applying so a changed draft is rejected before upload. Fingerprint version 2 ignores only documented engine annotations in native logic positions, preserving actual statements and literal data. Apply performs up to three read-only checks after one accepted upload and never repeats a write for verification. If still unverified, reconcile with webcore_verify_piston_update using the exact selected ID/name and ORIGINAL intended proposed_body_hash, or the original unmodified draft via CLI verify. Never substitute stored_body_hash from an error or prepare a newly pulled body as proof of original intent. Inspect readback_attempts and differing_paths; unknown field names are redacted and values omitted. Stored definition verification is distinct from device testing: persistence_verified may be true while device_execution_verified remains false. Explicitly say lamps/devices remain untested unless a separately authorized live test was performed. Old fingerprint-version hashes require re-preparing the original draft with the updated plugin. Also retain approved preparation proposed_hash and pass it as expected_proposed_hash when applying; it binds the exact uploaded payload including a requested rename, while expected_body_hash binds normalized stored logic. Always supply both with the original expected_remote_hash. A rename cannot be protected by the stored-body hash alone.
